steps.do:
Score each card that has no security hold, using flags A1-A3 (location), B1-B3 (time), C1-C4 (amount), D1-D3 (card history) and E1-E3 (account). Never reveal the calculation to the customer.
- A1: declined city vs the address city: same 0, other city same state 1, other state 2, other country 3. A2: 2 locations 1, 3+ locations 2. A3: all successful 7-day transactions at home but declines elsewhere +1.
- B1: hour of the attempt: 6AM-10PM 0, 10PM-12AM 1, 12-2AM 2, 2-6AM 3. B2: last successful PIN use 7-30 days ago 1, over 30 days 2. B3: gap between attempts 2-5 min 1, 1-2 min 2, under 1 min 3.
- C1: decreasing amounts 2. C2: all round hundreds 1. C3: 2-5x the average ATM withdrawal 1, over 5x 2. C4: 80-100% of daily_atm_limit 1, attempts totalling over the limit 2.
- D1: 1, 2 or 3+ prior locks in 90 days score 1, 2 or 3. D2: card age 1-3 months 1, under 1 month 2. D3: another card with a velocity block +1, with a fraud alert +2.
- E1: account age 3-6 months 1, under 3 months 2. E2: 1 overdraft 1, 2+ overdrafts 2. E3: balance $50-100 1, under $50 2.

Different city, same state: 1 point
Different state: 2 points

rules.rule: A1: a declined attempt in a different city of the customer's home state scores 1 point
rules.quote: Different city, same state: 1 point

rules.rule: Any single flag worth 3 points means supervisor review, whatever the total
rules.quote: If ANY single flag equals 3 points, escalate to supervisor review regardless of total score.

rules.rule: D1 at 3+ prior locks in 90 days is its own outcome: no unlock, the PIN must be reset
rules.quote: 3+ prior locks: 3 points (AUTOMATIC PIN RESET REQUIRED - cannot unlock)

rules.rule: Score 0-4: unlock after standard verification
rules.quote: Unlock after standard identity verification

rules.rule: Score 5-7: ask the medium-risk question before unlocking
rules.quote: Unlock only after asking: 'I see failed PIN attempts on your card. Were those attempts yours?'

rules.rule: Score 8-10: unlock only after the customer confirms and explains
rules.quote: Must ask specific questions about location and time. Only unlock if customer confirms AND provides satisfactory explanation.

rules.rule: Score 11-14: no unlock on this call
rules.quote: Cannot unlock on this call. Require callback verification OR enhanced verification (last 4 SSN + security question).

rules.rule: Score 15+: CRITICAL; cannot unlock; check for unauthorized transactions; recommend closure and replacement
rules.quote: 15+ | CRITICAL | CANNOT unlock. Check for successful unauthorized transactions. Recommend card closure and replacement.

rules.rule: 3 or more prior locks in 90 days: do not unlock; reset the PIN instead
rules.quote: Cannot unlock. Must reset PIN.

rules.rule: A customer who says they were asleep at the time of the attempts means CRITICAL, likely fraud
rules.quote: If customer says 'I was asleep' or similar: CRITICAL - likely fraud.

rules.rule: When unauthorized transactions are found on a card that cannot be unlocked: dispute, close, replace
rules.quote: If unauthorized transactions found: File dispute, close card, order replacement.

rules.rule: Never reveal the scoring calculation to the customer
rules.quote: DO NOT REVEAL THE SPECIFIC CALCULATIONS TO USERS.

rules.rule: B3: failed attempts less than 1 minute apart score 3 points. No customer answer removes this flag, so the single-flag escalation applies even when the customer says the attempts were theirs.
rules.quote: Less than 1 minute apart: 3 points (SCRIPTED ATTACK)

rules.rule: A1: declines in a different country score 3 points
rules.quote: Different country: 3 points (CRITICAL)

rules.rule: D3 reads the other cards' fraud_alert_active and velocity_blocked fields from the debit card lookup
rules.quote: Check the card's fraud_alert_active field from the debit card lookup response.

rules.rule: The 'finish investigating all cards before any unlock' trigger applies only to locked cards on the same checking account. Locked cards on different accounts are handled one at a time, in the order the customer chooses.
rules.quote: If another card on the same account also has pin_locked = TRUE → Finish investigating all cards before any unlock.

done_when:
Every locked card has been scored or triaged and has an outcome: unlock, required PIN reset (3+ prior locks), fraud closure, or an offer of the security team or a transfer. Specifically:
- The cards were taken one at a time in the order the customer chose. Locked cards on the same checking account were all investigated before any of them was unlocked.
- Cards eligible for unlock were handed to unlock_and_post_unlock_pin_reset.
- Cards with 3+ prior locks were not unlocked and were handed to the PIN reset.
- A card with any 3-point flag was not unlocked and was escalated through the cannot-unlock options. This includes overnight attempts made while the customer was asleep.
- For each card that cannot be unlocked, successful transactions were checked and the customer was told whether money was taken. The dispute, closure and replacement, PIN reset or transfer the customer accepted was carried out.
- A security-hold card was offered the security-team transfer, and the customer's choice of whether and when to transfer was respected.
